contract.note: Material obscuring of financial weakness is a fair ordinary reading without requiring fraud. The quarter, industry coverage, and materiality standard are evaluator-supplied.

evidence.note: The research supports a narrower disclosure-gap component: model-building costs were rarely disclosed. It does not establish underlying financial fragility or its material concealment.
CoreWeave publicly disclosed losses and profitability risks before the post. This company disclosure limits a blanket concealment reading but supplies no representative industry comparison.

reviews.rationale: Missing cost disclosures provide partial support, while CoreWeave demonstrates public risk disclosure. Neither establishes how representative disclosures compared with actual economic fragility. These narrower findings do not settle the industry-wide assertion.

contract.note: Subscription receipts versus attributable delivery costs is a fair reading in context. Leaving the historical start unspecified avoids inventing a date; the missing historical product data prevent resolution.

evidence.note: Reports an executive's admission about one subscription product at one time. The unspecified cost basis cannot establish persistent delivery-cost subsidies across both labs.
The company filing was available before the cutoff and covers historical finances. Aggregate positive gross profit includes consumption-based products and does not establish subscription margins.

reviews.rationale: A reported Pro loss episode cannot establish substantial subsidies throughout the claimed history. Anthropic's aggregate positive gross profit cannot disprove subscription losses. Comparable historical subscription receipts and delivery costs are missing.

contract.note: Included API-priced value is a fair reading of the surrounding token discussion. Treating 16 cents as a rough truncation of 16⅔ cents is reasonable, though it is not exact or nearest-cent rounding.

evidence.note: The contemporaneous company support disclosure gives $70 for $60 and $400 for $200. Excess-value ratios are 16⅔ cents and $1 per dollar, excluding additional usage; these are not actual loss margins.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair included-value reading and restored exclusion of extra usage, the disclosed allowances support the comparison. The first figure is approximate and the second exact. Supplier costs and actual financial losses remain unestablished.
